title: The Chauffeur's Club dixieland band and playing Snag It
summary: He played in Pat Powell's dixieland band with Isaac Jefferson and others, and answered Powell's punishing Snag It tempo with triple-tongued trumpet.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: What kind of band was that? Was that more of a jazz band and blues?
Yeah -- dixieland. We played strictly dixieland, because Powell was the leader then. James Powell was the leader and he played clarinet. And we really had a dixieland band.
Who else was in the band, do you recall?

Yeah. Isaac Jefferson, piano; Pat Powell, leader on clarinet; Dial Dyre was on drums; and, well, we had Lightfoot George Life at one time on saxophone, when Life left we had a boy by the name of [Swain] on the saxophone. And I was on the trumpet.
uh-huh. And what kind of tunes did you plan then? Did you play some blues by then?
Well, we played all kinds -- we played blues, we played 'Snag It' -- that's one of Louie's and Joe Oliver's numbers.
Yes. Did you play the break -- da-da-da-da-da-da-
Yes, but I played that when Pat Powell would get mad -- that was a tune he'd stomp off to punish you. He'd stomp 'Snag It' off this way -- one, two, three, four --
But you see, that didn't bother me -- that was triple tongue time you see -- di-di-di-di -- That's the way I played that you see, and that got him. I played triple tongue time, so --
Was Singleton Palmer around in those days?
Singleton Palmer -- tuba player. He might have come a little later.
He might have come a little later. I'll tell you who I met, though --
Yeah, Thigpen was around in those days. Now, this Thigpen that I hear of -- so much talk of, that must be his son.
I told my wife that was his son.
